extracted.intended_audience: Outstanding early-career scientists who require flexible working patterns (e.g., caring responsibilities or health-related conditions) and are applying for the Royal Society Dorothy Hodgkin Fellowship
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and eligibility/assessment criteria for applicants seeking the Royal Society Dorothy Hodgkin Fellowship — an eight-year fellowship aimed at enabling independent research careers for early-career scientists requiring flexible working. Covers who is eligible, what the award can fund, assessment and interview process, and available adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for flexible working due to personal circumstances (eligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: This scheme is for applicants who currently have, or will have by the start of the fellowship, a need for flexible support due to personal circumstances such as parental responsibilities, caring responsibilities, and/or clinically diagnosed health conditions that create a need for a flexible working pattern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must demonstrate the need for flexible support; this eligibility requirement is reviewed by the Grants team. Details about adjustments for disabled applicants are provided elsewhere on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early career stage (post-PhD experience limit)
rubrics_metrics.description: You should be in the early stages of your research career having up to six years of research experience since your PhD by the closing date of the round.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the scheme notes for further detail about the review of career breaks (i.e., how career interruptions are handled when counting the six-year limit).

rubrics_metrics.name: Must not hold a permanent post
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must not hold a permanent post (including proleptic appointment) in a university or not-for-profit organisation at the time of application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure your current contract status meets this requirement before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Must not hold or have previously held an equivalent independence-providing fellowship
rubrics_metrics.description: You must not hold, or have previously held, an equivalent fellowship that provides an opportunity to establish an independent research group and therefore independent research status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have previously held a fellowship that conferred independent research status, you are ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research within the Royal Society remit (subject eligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Your research must be within the Royal Society’s remit of natural sciences, which includes but is not limited to biological research and biomedical sciences, chemistry, engineering, mathematics and physics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the breakdown of subject groups and areas supported by the Royal Society for details; a new question in the Research Proposal section allows applicants to indicate whether their proposal is primarily in Biological Sciences or Physical Sciences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nationality and visa eligibility (Global Talent Visa)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants can be of any nationality and those requiring a visa are eligible to apply for a Global Talent Visa under the fast-track process of endorsement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you require a visa, applications remain eligible and the scheme supports relocation and visa costs (see funding guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application submission method
rubrics_metrics.description: You must apply through the Royal Society’s application and grant management system, Flexi-Grant®.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read the scheme notes and contact your host organisation Research Office if you have questions; follow the online form and the Research Proposal subject categorisation question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum award value and allowable exceedance for relocation/visa
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants can apply for up to a maximum of £1.87 million over eight years. The total grant cap may be exceeded in order to cover relocation/visa costs if this is well justified in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full funding details are in the scheme notes and Royal Society Funding Guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted use of funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds can cover contribution to the award holder’s salary; indirect and estate costs; equipment costs and research expenses including consumables, travel, etc.; contribution towards research assistance salary and associated indirect and estate costs; support for a new four-year PhD studentship(s); relocation and visa costs for the applicants and their dependants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to scheme notes/Royal Society Funding Guidance for detailed eligible costs and budgeting rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship length and mid-fellowship review requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowships are for eight years, with years six to eight being subject to satisfactory progress demonstrated in a mid-fellowship review at year four.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Progress in the first four years is assessed at the mid-fellowship review to determine continuation into years six to eight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision for flexible working patterns and leave
rubrics_metrics.description: The scheme provides flexibility to accommodate personal circumstances including part-time working for health reasons or caring responsibilities and provision for maternity, paternity, shared parental, adoptive or extended sick leave.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should describe how they will use flexible working arrangements where relevant; the scheme also provides financial support for childcare costs arising from conferences and research visits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career development and engagement opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Royal Society Research Fellows have access to tailored, high quality professional development, networking and engagement opportunities, including training on leadership, science communication and public engagement, and activities coordinated by science policy and schools engagement teams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are additional benefits of the fellowship intended to support development as a research leader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment confidentiality for declared need for flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Your need for flexibility will only be viewed by the Society’s Grants team to check your eligibility for the scheme; it will not normally be shared with panel members unless it becomes relevant to the assessment process, and only with your permission if sharing is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for adjustments are handled in confidence; contact dhf@royalsociety.org for confidential support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment workflow and decision-making stages
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment is overseen by the Dorothy Hodgkin Fellowship Panel. Following eligibility checks, applications are initially assessed by two panel members with the most appropriate scientific expertise; a longlist is drawn up; longlisted applications are subject to independent peer review; after peer review a shortlist for interview is drawn up with oversight from the Panel Chair; interviews are held and the Panel confirms recommendations for funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that multiple stages (eligibility, initial assessors, peer review, interview) influence selection; provide strong written case to succeed at each stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview format and aims
rubrics_metrics.description: Shortlisted applicants will be invited to an in-person interview at the Royal Society. The aim of the interview is for you to demonstrate the importance and scientific validity of your work and to describe how the award will lead to your scientific independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare to clearly articulate significance, scientific rigor and a realistic plan for achieving independence during the interview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support and adjustments for disabled applicants (types offered)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjustments can include, but are not limited to: extension of the deadline; additional support to complete the application form; receiving the application form in a different format (such as Word); support during interviews including technical support for accessibility software or services; additional costs that candidates may incur on account of their particular disability to attend an interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All requests are made in confidentiality; contact the Grants team (dhf@royalsociety.org or +44 20 7451 2666) to request adjustments and discuss specific needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity, Diversity and Inclusion (EDI) commitment in assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: The Royal Society recognises that diversity is essential for excellence in STEM and wants to encourage applications from the widest range of backgrounds, perspectives and experiences. The Society regularly reviews and revises policies and processes to embed EDI principles in all aspects of the grant making process and ensure all talented applicants have an equitable chance to succeed as per the assessment criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be aware that the process is intended to be equitable; for further detail consult scheme notes or guidance documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact and further information (support resources)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have further questions see the FAQs or contact the Grants Team at DHF@royalsociety.org or visit the contact us page. Downloads available include scheme notes, Conditions of Award, and FAQs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided contacts and downloadable scheme notes to confirm finer eligibility details, permitted costs, and assessment expectations before applying.
